title: Reliability Lattice: cross-functional SLO program outline
content:
Purpose
This is a working outline for a cross-functional reliability program we are calling the 'Reliability Lattice'. The goal is to create a lightweight, repeatable process teams can use to define, adopt, and iterate SLOs and operational guardrails without adding big process overhead.

Context and thesis
- We have many good SLO playbooks and runbooks across teams, but adoption is inconsistent: some services have deep runbooks + dashboards, others only a Slack alert.
- The lattice metaphor: instead of a top-down monolithal program, think of a 2D lattice of lightweight cells (service-level pilots) connected by shared primitives (error budget policy, common metrics definitions, alerting templates). Cells can grow/contract independently but stay compatible.

High-level objectives (3 months)
1) Ship a 4-service pilot that exercises the whole lifecycle: SLO design -> rollout -> error budget ops -> postmortem linkage.
2) Produce a minimal SLO toolkit: definition template, dashboard template, alerting rules, runbook stub, onboarding checklist.
3) Run two cross-team "SLO chemistry" workshops to align vocabulary and ownership patterns.
4) Measure impact: time-to-incident-resolution, frequency of oncall escalations due to noisy alerts, adoption rate.

Scope (what is in/out)
In scope: core infra-backed services, public-hosted endpoints, internal data pipelines supporting model serving. Focus on services that are customer-facing or cost-sensitive.
Out of scope for the pilot: large monolith refactors, new infra rollouts (those need separate coordination).

Stakeholders and roles
- Program lead: Asha Patel (SRE) — overall coordination, executive syncs.
- Product liaison: Priya Singh — feature prioritization and customer impact context.
- Engineering champions (one per pilot service): Diego Morales, Evan Carter, Marta Novak.
- Observability owner: Platform Observability team — dashboard templates, data retention guidance.
- Oncall ops: SRE rotations — responsible for error-budget driven throttles/escrow.
- Legal/security: consult when SLOs require PII-based signal telemetry.

Core deliverables
- SLO Definition Template (single-page): service purpose, key user journey, SLI definitions, target SLO, measurement windows, burn-rate thresholds.
- Dashboard template: 1) SLO health, 2) errors-by-class, 3) latency heatmap, 4) customer-impact indicator.
- Alerting rubric: recommended conditions for SLO vs infrastructure alerts, dedup rules, severity mapping.
- Runbook stub: immediate mitigations, mitigation owner, rollforward/rollback checklist, postmortem link field.
- Onboarding checklist: how to claim a lattice cell, 30/60/90 day milestones.

Pilot selection criteria (why these services)
- Moderate traffic so we see meaningful signal in 48 hours.
- Diverse tech stacks to validate the templates (http/frontend, async jobs, model inference).
- Willing engineering champion and capacity to iterate during pilot window.

Pilot timeline (12 weeks)
- Week 0 (kickoff): Align stakeholders, pick 4 pilot services, import baseline metrics.
- Weeks 1–2: SLO chemistry workshop #1 (vocab, sample walk-throughs), fill SLO definition template for each service.
- Weeks 3–4: Implement SLIs, wire dashboards, baseline error budgets.
- Weeks 5–8: Observe, tune, automate alerts, runbook drafting, simulate burn-rate events (synthetic load + failure injection where safe).
- Week 9: SLO chemistry workshop #2 (lessons, early wins, pain points).
- Weeks 10–12: Make program changes, finalize toolkit, executive summary, propose rollout schedule.

Communication cadence
- Weekly 30m sync (program+champions) Fridays 10:00am PT — status, blockers, risks.
- Biweekly incubator demo (show dashboards, runbook changes) — invited: platform, product, SRE.
- Slack channel: #reliability-lattice (day-to-day questions + links to artifacts).
- Exec update: every 4 weeks via short one-pager.

Success metrics (how we know this worked)
- Two of four pilot services maintain SLOs within target for 30 consecutive days or have documented action when violated.
- Reduction in pager noise for pilot services by >=30% (measured by alert counts pre/post).
- Time-to-onboard (service adopting templates to running dashboards) <= 4 weeks for at least 3 services.
- Playbook artifacts reused by >=2 other teams within 60 days.

Operational patterns and policies (proposed)
- Error budget policy: burn-rate > 3x for > 6 minutes -> trigger mitigation playbook; burn-rate sustained for > 30 minutes -> consider ramping down non-critical traffic via feature flags or throttles.
- Stewardship rotations: champions to nominate secondary steward so each lattice cell has at least two people who can act on budget burns.
- Canary / fallback: All SLO-affecting deployments must include a fallback plan and a canary monitored SLO.

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Observability telemetry mismatch across stacks. Mitigation: Observability team provides mapping guide + ingestion helper scripts.
- Risk: Engineering bandwidth. Mitigation: Keep templates minimal; SREs offer hands-on help for first two pilots.
- Risk: Noise from flaky SLIs. Mitigation: Add service-level SLI smoothing and small burn-rate buffers in pilot phase.

Open questions / TODOs
- Which metric store do we standardize on for long-term SLO history? (Prometheus vs metrics-service vs logs-derived). @Observability to advise.
- Need legal check for any SLOs that would imply contractual SLAs for customers. @Legal.
- Should we require a formal oncall runbook for every lattice cell before declaring an SLO "active"? (proposal: yes, minimal runbook).

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Kickoff meeting invite + agenda (Asha).
- Identify candidate services and champions (champions to confirm by Tue).
- Create Confluence index page and link templates (Diego).

Notes to self / rough ideas
- Consider a small "SLO badge" microservice that returns a machine-readable SLO status for each service — could be used by dashboards and external health checks.
- Think about a monthly "reliability retro" where multiple lattice cells share a one-slide story: what failed, what changed, what we learned.

Appendix: workshop structure (SLO chemistry)
- 30m: quick primer (SLI vs SLO vs SLA, burn-rate basics).
- 40m: hands-on split into service groups — fill SLO template for a single user journey.
- 20m: group shareouts + synthesis.

This is intentionally lightweight and iterative. Expect this doc to change after workshop #1.
